In the polygon shown, each side is perpendicular to its adjacent sides, and all \(28\) of the sides are congruent. The perimeter of the polygon is \(56.\) The area of the region bounded by the polygon is

In the \(xy\)-plane, consider the L-shaped region bounded by horizontal and vertical segments with vertices at \((0,0),\) \((0,3),\) \((3,3),\) \((3,1),\) \((5,1)\) and \((5,0).\) The slope of the line through the origin that divides the area of this region exactly in half is

mappings.rationale: Use the midpoints to determine the legs of triangles BCD and EFD, then subtract their areas from the rectangle.
The displayed overlap is triangle AGB. Add the two square areas and subtract this overlap once.
mappings.answerReason: Each square has area 100. Since G is the center of ABCD, its distance from AB is 5, so [AGB]=10×5/2=25. The covered area is 200−25=175.

mappings.rationale: Partition the stepped polygon into seven horizontal strips whose widths are multiples of the common side length.
mappings.answerReason: Each side has length 56/28=2. The strip widths, in side-length units, are 1, 3, 5, 7, 5, 3, 1. Hence the area is (1+3+5+7+5+3+1)×2²=100.

mappings.rationale: Apply equal-base-angle relationships in the three isosceles triangles and use the supplementary angles at P.
mappings.answerReason: Let ∠A=α. AP=PC gives ∠APC=180°−2α, so ∠BPC=2α. PC=CB then gives ∠ABC=2α. Since AB=AC, both base angles of ABC are 2α, yielding 5α=180° and α=36°.

mappings.rationale: Determine angle A from the triangle angle sum, double it to obtain the central angle subtending BC, and identify that angle as one regular-polygon sector.
mappings.answerReason: The angle relation gives 9∠A=180°, so ∠A=20°. Minor arc BC subtends a central angle of 40°. Thus 360°/n=40°, giving n=9.

mappings.rationale: Write the line as y=kx and impose the equal-area condition. Dissection or shoelace computes the areas, and the line's height at x=3 determines its slope.
mappings.answerReason: The total area is 3×3+2×1=11. For 1/3<k<1, the area below y=kx is 2+3(3k)/2. Setting this equal to 11/2 gives k=7/9, which satisfies the assumed intersection range.

mappings.rationale: At each central polygon vertex, its interior angle and the interior angles of two surrounding regular polygons fill a full turn.
mappings.answerReason: A regular decagon has interior angle 144°. Each surrounding polygon therefore has interior angle (360°−144°)/2=108°. Solving 180°(n−2)/n=108° gives n=5.

mappings.rationale: Convert the arc length to a central angle, obtain the inscribed angle at A, and bisect the isosceles triangle to express the side ratio using sine.
mappings.answerReason: Minor arc BC subtends r/r=1 radian. The condition AB>r places A on the major arc, so ∠BAC=1/2 radian. If M is the midpoint of BC, then sin(1/4)=BM/AB=BC/(2AB), giving AB/BC=1/(2sin(1/4)).
